assertion_audit.fails_if: Wrong canonical result, more than one git query, or omission of persistent short-answer writes; the full SHA comes from the fixture git rev-parse, independently of the resolver.
A missing citation returns a nonempty answer, misses are queried repeatedly, or a miss is persisted across processes.
The missing citation resolves unexpectedly or a HEAD change does not trigger the second query; the separate twenty-miss test establishes that a stable HEAD does cache.
The strict result is wrong or strict reads use the populated cache rather than making twenty git calls.
A ref is cached or persisted, does not resolve to the independently read initial SHA, or returns the stale SHA after the independently verified branch movement.
The stored answer is not reused after clearing process memory or either returned identity differs from git rev-parse.
A nonmatching hex branch is wrongly memoized, its canonical identity is wrong, or it is persisted.
A timeout is cached, returns a nonempty answer, or the strict timeout does not raise CrewError with instrument-fault wording and make its own query.

assertion_independence: No assertion compares a resolver echo to the same unverified input: short-input calls assert the full identity independently read with git; missing results use independently absent prefixes; call-count assertions observe actual wrapped subprocess calls.

limitations: The live plan asks for a post-landing 20-second follower trace; integration, follower reload and that observation remain coordinator work, explicitly deferred in the evidence fragment:17.
A fetched object without HEAD movement does not invalidate an in-process miss, an explicitly accepted live-plan constraint.
The compatibility logs carry six matching pre-existing failures on both revisions; none was triaged or repaired by this review.
